relation: Seminal budgeted information gathering in continuous space; budget is deterministic and no return reserve or uncertain cost.

title: Efficient Informative Sensing using Multiple Robots
summary: Seminal eSIP approximation algorithm for budget-constrained informative paths maximizing GP mutual information, with sequential allocation extending guarantees to multi-robot teams.
relation: Foundational budgeted multi-robot IPP; budget is a known path-length/energy limit and robots are not at risk.

title: Multirobot Persistent Monitoring: Minimizing Latency and Number of Robots With Recharging Constraints
summary: Multirobot persistent monitoring where robots with discharge time D must visit recharging depots; approximation algorithms minimize latency and team size.
relation: Battery is renewable and travel costs are known; addresses how many robots are needed under endurance limits rather than risk allocation.

title: Multi-Robot Informative Path Planning from Regression with Sparse Gaussian Processes
summary: Sparse-GP gradient-based multi-robot IPP in continuous environments that jointly optimizes informative paths under distance budgets and kinematic limits.
relation: Multi-robot IPP with distance budgets; cost is deterministic path length.

title: Learning Risk-Aware Costmaps for Traversability in Challenging Environments
summary: Neural network learns the CVaR (tail risk) of traversability costs from data to build risk-aware costmaps, motivated by preserving robot life in caves and subways.
relation: CVaR over uncertain per-cell cost, a template for risk-aware dose costmaps; no budget accounting or team.

title: Randomized algorithm for informative path planning with budget constraints
summary: Randomized Anytime Orienteering (RAOr) for budgeted IPP / correlated orienteering, posing it as CSP plus TSP for fast near-optimal online solutions.
relation: Budgeted orienteering with known edge costs; single robot, no risk.

title: Path-Based Sensors: Paths as Sensors, Bayesian Updates, and Shannon Information Gathering
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
summary: Treats whether a robot survives a path as a 'path-based sensor', derives the Bayesian update and expected Shannon information, and plans paths that learn about invisible robot-destroying hazards while also searching for victims.
relation: Formalizes the idea that the searcher's own damage/destruction is itself a measurement of the hazard, and that losing a robot destroys future information.

title: Learning about physical parameters: the importance of model discrepancy
summary: Shows that calibration ignoring model discrepancy yields biased and over-confident parameter estimates; a GP discrepancy fixes predictions but true parameters are recovered only with realistic priors.
relation: Theoretical explanation for the thesis's overconfident particle filter under spatially correlated model error.

title: A decentralized control policy for adaptive information gathering in hazardous environments
venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
summary: Decentralized MI-gradient controller for resource-constrained robots that localize an unknown number of targets while avoiding hazards at unknown positions that cause robot failure, using finite-set statistics and adaptive cell decomposition.
relation: Earlier decentralized version of the hazard-aware information-gathering framework; direct precedent for a team trading information against robot loss.

title: Probabilistic Multi-Robot Gas Source Localization with Uncalibrated Sensors: A Distributed Estimation Approach
summary: Distributed probabilistic framework where each robot estimates a local belief so that heterogeneous, uncalibrated sensors with inconsistent responses can still be fused for source localization.
relation: Addresses inconsistent measurement models in shared beliefs, related to model-error-driven overconfidence.

title: SniffySquad: Patchiness-Aware Gas Source Localization with Multi-Robot Collaboration
summary: Multi-robot olfaction system that accounts for patchy real-world gas distributions, which break reactive and simplified-plume-model methods that work in idealized simulations.
relation: Evidence that simplified dispersion models fail in real spatially structured fields, motivating discrepancy-aware estimation.

title: Bayesian Decentralized Decision-Making for Multi-Robot Systems: Sample-Efficient Estimation of Event Rates
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Multi-Robot and Multi-Agent Systems (MRS)
summary: A swarm decides which of two areas is safer, each with an unknown Poisson rate of hazardous events, using conjugate Bayesian estimates and confidence to reduce exposure while sampling.
relation: Explicitly treats measurement as costly exposure and seeks sample-efficient collective decisions, akin to declaring a source with limited dose.

title: Multi-source plume tracing via multi-agent reinforcement learning under common UAV-faults
summary: MARL (LSTM-based action-specific double deep recurrent Q-network) for a sUAS swarm localizing multiple airborne pollution sources in a Gaussian-plume POMG with sensor noise; journal version considers common UAV faults.
relation: Closest MARL plume-source paper; agents can fault but no hazard-dose budget.

title: Improved Socialtaxis for information-theoretic source search using cooperative multiple agents in turbulent environments
summary: Improves Socialtaxis with a continuous Rao-Blackwellized particle filter, a utility using distance to the estimated source to balance exploration/exploitation, sequential greedy decisions and connectivity preservation.
relation: Multi-agent information-theoretic source search with an explicit approach-the-source term; baseline for MARL comparisons.

title: Searching for a source without gradients: how good is infotaxis and how to beat it
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A
summary: Characterizes infotaxis performance from 1D to 4D in a POMDP framing and beats it with tree search, value-function heuristics and deep RL, which finds near-optimal policies.
relation: Supports using RL over hand-crafted information heuristics for source search.

title: Risk-Aware Path Planning for Unmanned Aerial Systems in a Spreading Wildfire
venue: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics
summary: Evidential fusion estimates wildfire state and flight-level heat aura under an inaccurate fire model; the UAV visits high-conflict locations and plans chance-constrained paths around a probabilistic keep-out zone.
relation: Hazard that damages the vehicle, uncertain hazard model, and information-seeking visits combined with risk constraints.

title: PDE solution to UAV/UGV trajectory planning problem by spatio-temporal estimation during wildfires
summary: UAV gathers camera information to estimate and predict wildfire spread with a POD-reduced Kalman filter, and UAV/UGV paths are planned with a PDE method that encodes wildfire threat as a risk function.
relation: Heterogeneous team estimating a vehicle-damaging hazard field while planning risk-averse paths.

title: Cooperative information-driven source search and estimation for multiple agents
summary: Multiple mobile sensors share minimal data and use a particle filter for source position and release rate; compares non-, passive and negotiated coordination of infotaxis.
relation: Close methodological analogue (shared particle filter + information-driven multi-agent search) without exposure cost.

title: Model-based gas source localization strategy for a cooperative multi-robot system—A probabilistic approach and experimental validation incorporating physical knowledge and model uncertainties
summary: Probabilistic PDE-based gas dispersion model with explicit model uncertainties for cooperative multi-robot exploration and gas source localization, with experimental validation (per title; abstract not returned).
relation: Explicitly incorporates physics-model uncertainty into multi-robot source estimation, relevant to filter overconfidence under model error.

title: Information-Based Search for an Atmospheric Release Using a Mobile Robot: Algorithm and Experiments
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
summary: Joint Bayesian estimation and information-gain planning for source term estimation with a ground robot, accounting for meteorological/dispersion parameter uncertainty and intermittent low-cost sensor readings; first experiments in turbulent conditions.
relation: Experimental single-robot analogue of source-term estimation with model-parameter uncertainty.

title: Autonomous Multi-Robot Search for a Hazardous Source in a Turbulent Environment
summary: Cognitive (infotaxis) multi-robot search for a toxic atmospheric release with Rao-Blackwellized Bayesian source estimation and scalable formation control under centralized replicated fusion.
relation: Direct non-nuclear analogue of shared-belief multi-robot source search; does not model harm to robots.

title: Multi-agent search for source localization in a turbulent medium
summary: Extends infotaxis to a distributed multi-agent team using relative entropy so that control actions maximize team information gain and speed up source localization.
relation: Foundational multi-agent infotaxis paper.

title: Bayesian Calibration of Inexact Computer Models
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
summary: Proposes a bias prior orthogonal to the gradient of the computer model to resolve the ill-defined parameter and suboptimally broad posterior in Kennedy-O'Hagan calibration.
relation: Methodological option for GP discrepancy in the source-location likelihood while keeping the location identifiable.

title: A Bayesian approach to improved calibration and prediction of groundwater models with structural error
summary: Integrates Gaussian process error models into Bayesian calibration of groundwater models; conventional least squares compensates structural error with parameters and gives biased, overconfident predictions.
relation: Applied demonstration that GP structural-error terms restore calibrated uncertainty in a spatial transport model.

title: Multi-robot gas leakage source localization based on deep reinforcement learning
summary: Multi-robot DRQN with CNN over image-like states and policy sharing for gas leak source localization as a POMDP, tested with 2-4 robots, obstacles and different wind speeds.
relation: Recent multi-robot deep RL gas-source baseline without exposure modeling.

title: Odor Source Localization in Obstacle Regions Using Switching Planning Algorithms with a Switching Framework
summary: OSL robots for hazardous chemical plumes in obstacle regions, where dispersion models are hard to build; switches planners to dynamically balance exploration and exploitation.
relation: Motivates exploration/exploitation switching when the plume model is unreliable.

title: Humanitarian demining for the clearance of landmine-affected areas
summary: Decision support model that produces safe and cost-effective mine detection search plans (exact linear methods and a genetic algorithm), since demining carries high risk to deminers and equipment.
relation: Search planning where the searcher can be harmed by what it is looking for.

title: Resilient Active Information Acquisition With Teams of Robots
summary: Receding-horizon multi-robot planner (RAIN) that maximizes information while being robust to attacks that disable robots' sensors, with suboptimality bounds via curvature.
relation: Robustness of team information gathering to losing members; background for team degradation when robots run out of budget.

title: Entrotaxis as a strategy for autonomous search and source reconstruction in turbulent conditions
summary: Sequential Monte Carlo estimation of source location and strength with a maximum-entropy-sampling reward (Entrotaxis), compared with infotaxis; faster and cheaper to compute in most scenarios.
relation: Alternative information objective for PF-based source search.

title: A review of source term estimation methods for atmospheric dispersion events using static or mobile sensors
summary: Review of source term estimation methods for atmospheric releases using static sensor networks and mobile sensors (per title; abstract not returned by tool).
relation: Survey reference for hazardous-release source estimation outside nuclear.

title: RESCUER: Development of a Modular Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Robot for Intervention, Sampling, and Situation Awareness
summary: Modular CBRN robot for intervention and sampling, designed around the need to decontaminate the robot after contamination in real missions.
relation: Practical evidence that CBRN exposure degrades or contaminates the robot itself.

title: Multi-Robot gas-source localization based on reinforcement learning
summary: Strategy-sharing multi-agent RL trains multiple robots for gas source localization in large-scale advection-diffusion plume simulations.
relation: Early MARL for gas-source search.

title: Projected needs for robot-assisted chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) incidents
summary: Cognitive work analysis with 20 domain experts, Fukushima lessons and hazmat literature to project how UAVs and UGVs can assist CBRN identification and containment.
relation: Operational motivation for robotic CBRN search teams.

title: Unmanned multi-robot CBRNE reconnaissance with mobile manipulation System description and technical validation
summary: Prototype multi-robot CBRNE reconnaissance system with modular sensor suites and a mobile manipulator for sampling in unknown environments.
relation: Systems-level example of a multi-robot CBRN team.
